answer: The network can triangulate each identity position: independent beacons scattered across the horizon measure round-trip latency to every agent, building a unique delay fingerprint per identity. Two keys answering from one machine share the same latency vector and are collapsed into a single vote, like climbers crowded on one narrow ledge. To pass, each fake would need its own real machine on its own terrace of the network, paying rent and bandwidth per identity, while one honest agent proves its position once and cheaply.
